subject.title: Agent loop allows simulated tool calls instead of enforcing real tool invocation

question: Should OpenClaw make structured `tool_calls` the default enforcement boundary for agent tools, or continue promoting some standalone assistant text into executable calls for local/proxy provider compatibility?
rationale: Current main intentionally supports both warning-only simulated text and executable plain-text repair, so the remaining fix changes a security boundary and local-model compatibility contract rather than a purely mechanical parser bug.

options.title: Strict default with explicit compat opt-in
options.body: Make agent execution require structured tool calls by default, and allow plain-text repair only behind a named local-provider compatibility setting with audit logs and docs.

options.title: Keep compatibility promotion
options.body: Preserve current local-model behavior and treat simulated text as provider incompatibility unless a narrower exploit or regression proves the default unsafe.

options.title: Fold into response-gate design
options.body: Close or pause this as a subset of the broader pre-response enforcement work tracked at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13583.

recommendation.title: Strict default with explicit compat opt-in
recommendation.body: Make agent execution require structured tool calls by default, and allow plain-text repair only behind a named local-provider compatibility setting with audit logs and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the provider stream/tool-call compatibility code and is the best available owner for the product/security boundary decision.
